$comment: Thursday's working-indicator phrases. DATA, not code: adding a phrase, retuning the interval, or banning a new word all happen in this file, and tests/ enforces every constraint over it, so a phrase that breaks a rule fails the suite rather than shipping. See ticket TH3.

rotation.$comment: TH3 requires an interval of at least 2.5 seconds. MINIMUM_INTERVAL_MS in src/rotation.ts is the floor the code enforces; intervalMs is the value we actually ship, and a test asserts it clears the floor. Raising it here needs no code change; lowering it below the floor fails the suite.

phrases: Assuming you meant the hard one
Looking for what holds it up
Sorting the useful from the loud
Putting it in a sensible order

vocabulary.$comment: The words a phrase may not contain, grouped by the criterion each group enforces. Matching is on WORD TOKENS, not substrings: a phrase is lowercased and split on every non-letter, so 'load-bearing' yields 'load' and 'bearing' and is caught, while 'thoroughly' does not match 'thor'. Extending a list here needs no code change, which is the same property criterion 8 asks of the phrase list itself.

mythology.$comment: Criterion 2. Thursday is the assistant, not the weekday and not the god. This list covers the Norse figures, the thunder imagery, and the etymological chain behind the day's name in both the Germanic (Thunor/Donar) and Romance (Jove/Jupiter) branches, because 'Jove's day' is the same criterion wearing a different hat.

toolNames.$comment: Criterion 6, the 'tool' half. Every one of these is the literal name of a tool an agent in this harness can call, so a phrase containing one reads as a claim that the tool is running. There is no tool registry in this workspace to harvest from yet (packages/aidos is a README), so this list is AUTHORED and reviewable rather than derived; when a registry lands, tests/phrases.test.ts should cross-check against it and this comment should go away.

modelNames.$comment: Criterion 6, the 'model' half. Naming a model is the most brittle thing a phrase can do -- it dates the product, and it may simply be untrue of the session the user is in.

systemNouns.$comment: Criterion 6, the 'file' half, plus the machinery a file lives in. This is the load-bearing list: a phrase can only CLAIM a specific operation if it names the thing the operation is done to, so banning the objects makes the unnamed-verb residue harmless. Deliberately absent: 'note' and 'notes', which are as ordinary as they are technical, and 'order' and 'answer' for the same reason. Those are judgement, not mechanism, and the TH3 report says so out loud.

operations.$comment: Criterion 6, the 'operation' half, and the ONLY part of that criterion that is fully mechanical. Every word here names a computing operation and has no ordinary use in this register, so banning it costs nothing. Verbs that are operations only in context -- sorting, counting, checking, holding, putting -- are deliberately NOT here: banning them would ban the voice the ticket asks for, and they cannot claim a specific operation while systemNouns forbids naming a thing to perform it on. That residue is an admitted gap, restated in tests/phrases.test.ts.
